headline: Learned models of neural and neuroimaging data are tested for attribution and transfer
label: Learned Models Of Neural Activity
summary: Recent preprints pair population-level and neuroimaging models with checks on whether pretraining, retrieval, and attribution claims hold up across datasets…
synthesis: The common thread is the use of learned models to extract structure from neural population activity, EEG, fNIRS, and resting-state connectivity. Several items test whether learned representations hold up rather than assuming them. A retrieval-augmented GAE framework classifies Parkinson's disease from resting-state functional connectivity, where pretraining raises accuracy from 60.5% to 66.0% but retrieval gains are inconsistent. A montage-aware masked autoencoder pretrained on 12 public fNIRS datasets targets transferable neurovascular representations. On the modeling side, Neural-DISCO performs source-conditioned counterfactual editing of population activity, a recurrent study examines multitask interactions across 100 cognitive tasks, a neuron-identity framework groups neurons into latent populations, and Predictive Brain Networks use local predictive-coding learning and are compared against vision models. What is new is the pairing of model construction with explicit evaluation of whether transfer and attribution claims survive scrutiny. The set is heterogeneous, so this pairing is not uniform across all six items.
